message:
Fix the map marker, quiet the log, unify the correction wording

THE PLAYER MARKER WAS NEVER A DRAWING PROBLEM. Every poll was succeeding --
ok:true in 39-63ms -- while the canvas had zero marker pixels. The bridge's
serializer %q-quotes STRING returns, so `return "x,y,z"` arrives as
"\"x,y,z\"" with the quotes as literal content. parseFloat('"2701.08') is NaN,
the isFinite guard bailed, and `player` stayed null for as long as the feature
had existed. The `r.value === "nil"` compare was dead for the same reason: that
is a string return too. Only strings are quoted -- numbers come back bare --
which is why it survives casual testing. Now goes through IDE.lua.unquote, the
helper the inspector was already using. Verified against the live game: the
marker lands at (107,101), within a pixel of where the edge calibration says it
should. It also gained a contrasting outline, because a 2px dot in one colour
was a speck at fit zoom and vanished outright into the colour relief's water.

THE LOG FLOOD HAD A CAUSE WORTH FIXING AT THE SOURCE. The bridge broadcasts
every Loader.WsSend to ALL connected clients, so a tagged result line belonging
to another IDE tab matched nothing pending here and was reported as mod
telemetry. Measured: two established connections to :27050, every tagged line
delivered to both, four stray lines per capture window. ess-bridge.js now drops
tagged lines that are not its own -- four to zero in the same window. Hiding
them alone would have papered over it.

On top of that, raw ws pushes are hidden by default behind a toggle, and the
two kinds get SEPARATE ring buffers. Sharing one 600-line ring meant a chatty
mod evicted every real log line while its own sat hidden: a log that looks
empty because of traffic you asked not to see.

MAP POLLING drops to 4s and skips entirely when the map is not the active panel
or the tab is backgrounded. It is a helper panel, not a telemetry feed. (That
gate is real: first verification showed no polls at all until document.hidden
was checked.)

TELEPORT CLEARANCE 1.5 -> 5. The height grid samples once per 32 world units
(cell 16 x coarseStep 2), so on a slope the ground under the exact spot clicked
can sit well above the sample and 1.5 put you inside the hillside. Overshooting
costs a short fall; undershooting costs a stuck character.

ONE VOCABULARY FOR THE GROUNDING CHECK. Agent mode and plain chat reported the
same finding in different words -- and the mismatch was not only wording. Agent
mode said a name "was not in any source it had been shown", which is the weak
pack-level claim, while plain chat had already resolved it against the full
wiki index first. The more alarming phrasing was attached to the weaker
evidence. Both now run the same classify() and render from the same three
verdicts in 85_ground.js (absent / elsewhere / unverified). Consequence beyond
wording: agent mode no longer interrupts for names that are real and merely
outside the loaded pack, which on the small tiers is most of what the check
flags -- it used to spend a round trip telling the user their correct answer
was correct.

ALSO: .clr buttons were rendering with the UA button face, measured
rgb(240,240,240) on an rgb(11,16,23) panel -- the "rules" button was a light
grey blob in dark mode, while the "clear" span beside it was transparent
because it is a span. And draw() now bails without a 2D context instead of
throwing, which is what the new dock hook exposed in the jsdom harness.

214 smoke tests, up from 199. The new ones cover the quoting bug in both
directions (NaN without unquoting, parsed with), the foreign-tagged-line drop,
the ws toggle and the flood-eviction guarantee, and that an agent correction
renders the identical sentence plain chat would have shown.
